g.text: LLTS — Low-Latency Transport for CrownOS continuity
Linux laptop ⇄ Android device · screen / camera / mic / input · LAN Wi-Fi or USB · ≤ 12 ms protocol latency · every number below is taken from the source (crates/llts-*)
1 · Architecture — two devices, one protocol stack
Linux laptop and Android phone run byte-identical sans-I/O logic; only the bottom (sockets) and top (codecs, UI) differ.
per-vendor Linux backends (README; not yet in workspace)
JNI bridge — 21 natives · commands in · JSON events out
Surfaces handed over, never media bytes

UDP — one unconnected socket, :47470 on Android
logical peer link: Capabilities · Subscribe/Update · Start* / OpenStream · commands
(rides the reliable channel inside the sealed datagrams)
audio · input · control · feedback · probes · handshakes
llts-bench — two PeerSessions over real loopback UDP, synthetic encoder
25 kB frames · 60 Hz · 12 Mbit/s → p99 encode-submit → presented
CI gate: p99 ≤ 12 ms, every frame presented · measured p99 4.9 ms clean, 6.3 ms @5 % loss
Pair once, then every reconnect is a single Noise IK round trip triggered by a private beacon.
Beacons carry no name and no stable id: a stranger sees random bytes, a linked device sees who it is.
epoch u64 LE) · epoch = unix/900 s
the file-share stack on first Connected
Linked advertisement — 24 B (fits a legacy BLE PDU)
Pairing beacon — 12 B (only while a pairing window is open)
flags: NEARBY_CODE → Noise XX + 6-digit code · QR → Noise XXpsk3
nonce identifies the window, not the device · DeviceClass: Phone 1 · Tablet 2 · Watch 3 · Computer 4
Beacon heard on BLE or mDNS
precomputed for every link over epoch ±1
epoch byte outside window? rebuild once with ±4
Noise is used only to agree keys; datagrams are then sealed by the llts key schedule.
both show code = derive_key("…pairing verification code",
hash || N_i || N_r) → u64 mod 10⁶ → 6 digits
users confirm within 60 s → Paired + Connected
scanner: responder static key == QR static_key
wrong PSK fails inside Noise · trusted at once → Paired + Connected
authorize(): static key in TrustStore AND
listener commits on the first authenticated packet
simultaneous dial: lower static key wins
body: pattern u8 (0 XX · 1 XXpsk3 · 2 IK)
message_index u8 · sender_tag u16 · Noise ≤512 B
responder never resends, caches its reply
for a resent msg 0, gives up after 10 s
token buckets on first messages only:
per source IP burst 4, +1 / 250 ms (64 IPs)
Every datagram: 28 B clear header (authenticated as AAD) · encrypted body · 16 B Poly1305 tag.
Nonce (12 B, never sent — rebuilt from header)
counter u64 LE ← u16 seq extended by rollover
root || direction (1 I→R · 2 R→I) || stream_id u32 || epoch u32)
one key per (direction, stream, epoch) · rekey 120 s or 2³² packets
KEY_PHASE = epoch & 1 · retired key kept 3 s · ≤ 16 streams / direction
receive: peek → decrypt (guess, guess+65536) → replay 1024 bit → commit
loss ‰ u16 · n × {transport_seq u16, arrival µs u32, ecn u8}
n × {first u16, extra u8} — covers extra+1 sequences
BodyPrefix · channel_seq u16 · cumulative_ack u16 · body
token u32 · n u8 · n × {stream u32, space u8, counter u64} · pad
token u32 · probe_arrival u32 · ack_departure u32
pattern u8 · message_index u8 · sender_tag u16 · Noise msg
RepairBlockGeometry: first_data_index u16 · data_shard_count u16 · shard_bytes u16 (even) · block_byte_offset u32 · block_byte_len u32
parity_index = packet_index − data_shard_count · one Reed-Solomon block per encoded slice
Input payload (inside Media kind): batch_count u8, then {sequence u16, events_len u16, events} newest first; KEYFRAME = key-state snapshot
Sizing: MTU 1200 − (28 header + 4 prefix + 14 geometry + 16 tag = 62) → 1138 B payload, even for RS shards
u16 sequence / frame_id wrap; a < b ⇔ (a − b) as i16 < 0 · version = 1, peers must match · session_tag 0 = unassigned
6 · Media data path — one video stream, end to end
Top: sender, left → right. Right: the network. Bottom: receiver, right → left. Middle: the feedback loops.
rebuild: RETRANSMISSION flag, new seq in
Retx space (no nonce reuse), original_seq in prefix

Audio (Opus, 10 ms): no parity, no NACK, delivered immediately · Input: each packet repeats the last 4 batches, receiver dedups by batch sequence, key-state snapshot on change and every 500 ms · Nack, Feedback, Probe, ProbeAck skip the pacer.
Delay gradient drives the rate; measured loss and RTT decide how much parity and whether to NACK.
provisioned = (E + √(9E)) / k, E = ⌈loss · k⌉ (mean + 3σ of a binomial)
parity shards = ⌈rate · k⌉, ≥ 1 if rate > 0 · max 50 % · then clamp [min, max]
loss is the peer-reported ‰ from transport feedback

Pure (now, event) → actions state machine: SliceEncoded · DatagramReceived · ControlQueued · InputQueued · TimerExpired … → Transmit · PresentFrame · Deliver · SetTargetBitrate · PeerDead · ArmTimer …
delayed ACK 2 ms (now on gap / dup)
every packet repeats the last 4 batches
Probe every 1 s idle, 250 ms with media
(media counts as active 1 s after a frame)
keep the min-RTT sample of every 8
authenticated traffic from a new path
switch only on a matching ack
Sans-IO: runtime feeds NodeInput → Node::handle, executes every NodeOutput, calls back on next_timeout. bridge.rs maps to/from the Driver.
transport brings up the first session
Feature negotiation — the encoder always proposes
peer: feature enabled & not active? else Stop · codec = own preference ∩ peer list
stream index parity: lower DeviceId uses even, higher odd · OpenMedia(Sender) → Proposed
OpenStream{index, purpose, VideoParams{codec, w, h, fps, kbps}}
Mirror ToPeer / Monitor: requester is the encoder and proposes right after Start*
State sync — each device owns its documents, nothing is merged
queues a set of dirty topics
Capabilities{codecs, features, class} on Control 0 → shared = local ∩ enabled ∩ peer → Subscribe / Unsubscribe topics
Subscribe → Snapshot (authoritative, clears absent topics; spills into Updates if > 64 KiB)
topics: DeviceInfo · Battery · MediaSession · CallState · Notifications · Clipboard · Volume · Hotspot (u16 bitmask)
clipboard winner = max(HLC{wall_ms, counter}, origin DeviceId) · inline ≤ 60 KiB, else an ffsp file offer
[msg_type u16 LE][postcard body] · unknown type → skipped · < 0x0100 reserved for transport (KeyframeRequest 0x0001)
OpenStream{index, purpose, Video|Audio params} · AcceptStream{stream, codec} · CloseStream{stream}
Call{Pickup|Decline|Hangup|Dial} · Media{Play|Pause|Next|Prev|Seek} · Reply · SetVolume · Lock · SetHotspot · FileOffer
StartMirror{direction, limits, remote_input} · StartCamera · StartMic · StartMonitor · UnicursorEnter/Leave · Stop
Pairing in the node · QR: BeginPairing → window{120 s, nonce} + OfferQrPairing + pairing beacon → QrOfferReady → PairingOffer{uri} · scanner: PairWithQr → PairWithOffer
Nearby: both windows open → lower window nonce starts PairNearby → PairingCode → PairingRequest{code} → user confirms (auto-reject after 60 s, ≤ 4 pending)
Paired → adopt peer (default features, Persist) · close window · refresh beacons · ExportFfspLink on first Connected · Forget → Goodbye(Unpaired), peer forgets too
Kotlin owns the platform, Rust owns the protocol. Only small, cold data crosses JNI — media goes MediaCodec ↔ socket directly.
① ppoll [driver fd, wake fd], timeout = min(driver, node)
⑥ route driver events → node · media · input JSON
⑧ drain_node: Driver · App JSON · Media · Persist · Advertise
NDK persistent input Surface · async callbacks →
I-frame 60 s (keyframes on demand), realtime priority
renders to view Surface, low-latency=1 · no free input
buffer → park keyframe, drop others · no surface yet
AAudio exclusive, low latency, 48 kHz mono i16
Opus VoIP 32 kb/s, in-band FEC · 10 ms frames
Opus decode on runtime thread → 4-frame (40 ms)
playout queue, force_push · silence on underrun
